blogs.title: From LSTMs to xLSTMs: Giving Recurrent Networks a Modern Makeover
blogs.description: A story‑telling look at why classic LSTMs fell out of favor after Transformers arrived, and how the new xLSTM architecture revives the power of recurrent models for today’s large‑scale language tasks.

blogs.title: Exponential Gating Unpacked: How xLSTM Learns to Forget—and Remember—Better
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into the paper’s core innovation—exponential gating—explaining in plain language how it lets an RNN revise past decisions, solve nearest‑neighbor search problems, and overcome one of the biggest LSTM weaknesses.

blogs.title: Memory 2.0: Scalar vs. Matrix Memory in sLSTM and mLSTM
blogs.description: Compare the two new memory cells introduced in xLSTM: the scalar sLSTM with clever mixing across heads, and the matrix‑based mLSTM that stores key‑value pairs like a fast associative memory. Includes visual analogies to help readers grasp the difference.

blogs.title: Building a Giant from Tiny Bricks: Residual xLSTM Blocks vs. Transformer Layers
blogs.description: Explain how the authors embed sLSTM/mLSTM cells into residual block backbones, why up‑projection matters, and how stacking these blocks yields architectures that rival Transformer stacks while keeping linear time‑complexity.

blogs.title: Scaling LSTMs to Billions of Parameters: xLSTM’s Performance on Language Modeling Benchmarks
blogs.description: Summarize the experimental results—validation perplexity, long‑range arena scores, PALOMA domain tests—and show how xLSTM matches or beats state‑of‑the‑art Transformers and State‑Space Models when scaled up.

blogs.title: Parallelism vs. Mixing: Understanding the Speed Trade‑offs in sLSTM and mLSTM
blogs.description: Break down why sLSTM’s memory mixing prevents full parallel execution, how the authors built fast CUDA kernels, and why mLSTM can run in parallel despite its heavy matrix operations.

blogs.title: Why xLSTM Could Be a Game‑Changer for Edge AI and Long‑Context Applications
blogs.description: Discuss practical implications: constant memory usage over sequence length, linear compute cost, suitability for on‑device inference, and scenarios where long context retention matters—like code evaluation or time‑series forecasting.
